grading.A: primary official source or directly inspectable authoritative technical evidence
grading.A-: strong primary research/code evidence with stated limitations
grading.B+: useful research/open code but limited independent replication
grading.B/B-: concrete implementation or issue evidence with modest adoption/sample size

sources.title: Claude for Creative Work
sources.verification: Primary official announcement; capabilities are described by the vendor, not independently benchmarked.
sources.claim: Blender MCP is an officially available natural-language interface to Blender Python API and documentation; intended uses include scene analysis, scripts, plugins, procedural animation, parametric models and batch work.
sources.agent_use: Confirms that API-driven Blender assistance is a legitimate workflow, but does not prove expert modeling quality.
sources.adopted: Yes: semantic API, scripting, tutoring and repetitive-task positioning.

sources.title: ahujasid/blender-mcp
sources.verification: Public source code and observable repository activity; README claims are maintainer-authored.
sources.claim: Socket-based MCP bridge, scene inspection, screenshots, object/material control, arbitrary Blender Python execution, asset-service integrations; roughly 23k stars and 2.3k forks at snapshot.
sources.agent_use: Strong popularity and implementation reference. Use one server instance, explicit health checks, privacy settings, and semantic wrappers; popularity is not proof of modeling fidelity.
sources.adopted: Existing connection retained; no replacement bundled. Added optional Python pin/telemetry/one-instance hardening guidance.

sources.title: Blender MCP commands timeout on Windows 11 with Blender 5.1
sources.verification: Concrete user report with environment and logs; not a controlled benchmark.
sources.claim: Connection can appear active while tool calls time out on Blender 5.1.
sources.agent_use: Requires health checks, structured timeouts and retry/abort semantics.
sources.adopted: Yes: compatibility probe and failure policy.

sources.title: Incomplete JSON response, MCP timeout
sources.verification: Concrete logs; single-user report.
sources.claim: Long waits and truncated/incomplete JSON can break scene inspection.
sources.agent_use: Do not retry blindly; use bounded retries and idempotent operations.
sources.adopted: Yes: structured error categories in staged state.

sources.title: Arbitrary File Read via generate_hunyuan3d_model
sources.verification: Detailed reproducible vulnerability report; issue later closed as completed.
sources.claim: Unvalidated local paths in an external-generation tool enabled arbitrary readable files to be encoded and sent to an API.
sources.agent_use: Local path allowlisting and network-off-by-default are required.
sources.adopted: Yes: security preflight and path policy; not claimed as a complete sandbox.

sources.title: Vision-as-Inverse-Graphics Agent via Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning (VIGA)
sources.verification: Detailed method, benchmark and ablations; preprint and primarily author-evaluated.
sources.claim: Code-render-inspect loop, high-level semantic skills, strict observation/modification separation and bounded multimodal memory improve long-horizon graphics work.
sources.agent_use: Directly supports read-only inspection tools, short memory and targeted edits.
sources.adopted: Yes: core v4 architecture.

sources.title: Thinking in Blender: Staged Executable Inverse Graphics with Vision-Language Models
sources.verification: Method, experiments and limitations are explicit; very recent preprint without broad independent replication.
sources.claim: Separate geometry, material, composition and lighting stages; use a scoped verifier and explicit approval checklist for each stage.
sources.agent_use: Prevents material edits from damaging geometry and reduces cross-stage confusion.
sources.adopted: Yes: stage permissions, budgets, commits and optional global review.

sources.title: BlenderGym: Benchmarking Foundational Model Systems for Graphics Editing
sources.verification: 245 task instances, human baselines and verifier study; preprint.
sources.claim: Current VLM systems lag human Blender users; API mismatch, non-executable scripts and unreliable visual verifiers remain major failure modes.
sources.agent_use: Use compatibility tests, multiple views, structural QA and occasional human A/B choice rather than one visual metric.
sources.adopted: Yes: candidate selection and non-visual QA.

sources.title: 3DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agentic Procedural 3D Modeling Via Code
sources.verification: Large benchmark and human preference arena; very recent preprint.
sources.claim: Failures mostly come from API mismatches; even successful renders may contain disconnected or floating components; more reasoning and multi-turn refinement help.
sources.agent_use: Adds version probes, connection graph checks and a refinement budget.
sources.adopted: Yes: compatibility and assembly QA.

sources.title: BlenderRAG: High-Fidelity 3D Object Generation via Retrieval-Augmented Code Synthesis
sources.verification: 500 expert-validated examples and reported ablations; author-reported results, young public codebase.
sources.claim: Retrieving similar text/code/image examples improved reported compilation success and semantic similarity without fine-tuning.
sources.agent_use: Store compact verified examples and retrieve only top matches.
sources.adopted: Yes: dependency-free local example index; external vector DB remains optional.

sources.title: MaxRondelli/BlenderRAG
sources.verification: Public code; around 12 stars, 1 fork and 41 commits at snapshot.
sources.claim: Implements local retrieval with a vector database and executes generated scripts in Blender.
sources.agent_use: Useful implementation reference, but adoption is currently small.
sources.adopted: Concept only; no Qdrant dependency bundled.

sources.title: LL3M: Large Language 3D Modelers
sources.verification: Research system with examples and experiments; preprint.
sources.claim: Specialized agents plan, retrieve, write, debug and refine interpretable Blender Python using bmesh, modifiers and shader nodes.
sources.agent_use: Supports role separation and editable procedural code.
sources.adopted: Partially: planner/executor/reviewer roles, not a large permanent agent swarm.

sources.title: SceneCraft: An LLM Agent for Synthesizing 3D Scene as Blender Code
sources.verification: Method and evaluation; preprint.
sources.claim: A scene graph, numerical spatial constraints, render feedback and a reusable function library support complex scenes with many assets.
sources.agent_use: Create a scene graph before code and learn reusable functions rather than memorizing chat.
sources.adopted: Yes: scene graph schema and reusable example records.

sources.title: 3D-GPT: Procedural 3D Modeling with Large Language Models
sources.verification: Early research prototype; older model generation and limited modern MCP relevance.
sources.claim: Task dispatch, conceptualization and modeling agents can decompose procedural modeling tasks.
sources.agent_use: Supports simple role decomposition.
sources.adopted: Concept only; kept to three logical roles, not separate always-on agents.

sources.title: From Idea to Co-Creation: A Planner-Actor-Critic Framework for Agent Augmented 3D Modeling
sources.verification: Systematic comparison claimed, but limited independent replication and recent preprint.
sources.claim: Planner-Actor-Critic with human supervision outperforms a direct single-prompt workflow in reported geometry, aesthetics and task completion.
sources.agent_use: Give critic a checklist and allow user approval at ambiguous decisions.
sources.adopted: Yes: lightweight roles and human checkpoint, not conversational bureaucracy.

sources.title: 3Dify: Procedural 3D-CG Generation Assisted by LLMs Using MCP and RAG
sources.verification: Research proposal and system description; limited independent validation.
sources.claim: MCP + RAG + user selection among candidates can reuse preferred parameter patterns; local LLMs are possible.
sources.agent_use: Keep a small preference log and generate alternatives only where uncertainty is high.
sources.adopted: Yes: optional A/B candidate records.

sources.title: Proc3D: Procedural 3D Generation and Parametric Editing
sources.verification: Author-reported benchmarks; representation differs from this kit.
sources.claim: A compact procedural graph with exposed parameters enables fast edits without regenerating the whole object.
sources.agent_use: Prefer editable parameters, named parts and modifier stacks over destructive final meshes.
sources.adopted: Yes: parametric representation policy.

sources.title: Blendify — Python rendering framework for Blender
sources.verification: Public framework and technical report; focused more on rendering than modeling.
sources.claim: A high-level API reduces native Blender API complexity for scene creation, colors, materials and rendering.
sources.agent_use: Supports semantic wrappers instead of raw bpy everywhere.
sources.adopted: Already aligned with toolkit design.

sources.title: EZBlender: Efficient 3D Editing with Plan-and-ReAct Agent
sources.verification: Research benchmark and claims; recent preprint.
sources.claim: Global planning plus reactive local autonomy can reduce latency/cost while preserving editing quality.
sources.agent_use: Plan once, then use small local corrections rather than replanning the whole project.
sources.adopted: Yes: stage plan plus targeted attempt loop.

sources.title: Blender MCP Assembly Skill
sources.verification: Open instructions and before/after example; around 30 stars at snapshot; no large benchmark.
sources.claim: Connection planning, world-space bounds, overlap checks, transform application and final audits reduce disconnected assemblies.
sources.agent_use: Directly addresses floating fingers, tubes, chair parts and mascot components.
sources.adopted: Yes: independently implemented structural audit and connection graph.

sources.title: Blender MCP + AI AGNO Multi-Agent Production Studio
sources.verification: Open code and README; about 48 stars; demo link remains a placeholder in README.
sources.claim: Proposes 17 specialized agents and persistent memory across a full production pipeline.
sources.agent_use: Shows specialization is feasible, but does not establish that 17 agents are efficient or necessary.
sources.adopted: No: rejected as default due to context, cost and orchestration overhead.

sources.title: saofund/LLM-Blender-Agent
sources.verification: Public code; about 29 stars, 6 forks and 56 commits at snapshot.
sources.claim: Supports multiple LLM providers, function calling, Gradio, assets and external text/image-to-3D services.
sources.agent_use: Useful connector/provider reference; external generators do not replace editable procedural modeling.
sources.adopted: No external model services bundled.

sources.title: sandraschi/blender-mcp
sources.verification: Public code with tests and 108 commits; about 14 stars at snapshot.
sources.claim: A broader tool suite can support headless/live Blender, exports, VSE, geometry nodes and other workflows.
sources.agent_use: Shows headless testing and explicit tool families are practical.
sources.adopted: Concept only; no replacement server bundled.

sources.title: 3D Agent for Blender
sources.verification: Marketing claims and selected testimonials; no independent benchmark located.
sources.claim: Claims broad model support and faster creation workflows.
sources.agent_use: Demonstrates market interest, not proof of reliable expert-grade output.
sources.adopted: No vendor code or claims imported.

sources.title: Community discussion of AI-driven Blender modeling
sources.verification: Anecdotal community discussion; identities, setups and success criteria vary.
sources.claim: Users describe fast concept/blockout gains but acknowledge organic sculpting, precise CAD and polished characters remain difficult.
sources.agent_use: Sets realistic expectations: strong for structured blockout and iteration, weak as autonomous master sculptor.
sources.adopted: Yes: scope boundaries documented.

sources.title: Reddit feedback: Blender MCP / Claude modeling
sources.verification: Anecdotal, self-selected reports; often missing exact prompts, versions and output files.
sources.claim: Positive reports emphasize editable low-poly props and automation; negative reports mention poor spatial reasoning, primitive-looking objects and slow iteration.
sources.agent_use: Explains why reproducible logs, versions, references and acceptance tests matter.
sources.adopted: Feedback informs failure taxonomy only.

sources.title: AI Agent Creates 3D Models in Blender from Text (MCP Tutorial)
sources.verification: Linked by the main repository; video is a demonstration, not a controlled evaluation.
sources.claim: Shows installation and prompt-driven Blender operations.
sources.agent_use: Useful for setup and interaction patterns; convert only verified steps into skills.
sources.adopted: Indexed, not transcribed or treated as training data.

sources.title: Blender MCP setup instruction video
sources.verification: Linked by repository installation documentation.
sources.claim: Demonstrates connector setup.
sources.agent_use: Installation only; no evidence of complex modeling competence.
sources.adopted: Indexed for human setup.

sources.title: Blender MCP Assembly Skill tutorial
sources.verification: Linked from an open skill repository with inspectable instructions.
sources.claim: Explains connection planning, bounds, overlap and transform auditing.
sources.agent_use: Good candidate for converting video lessons into explicit checks.
sources.adopted: Concept reproduced independently in v4 structural QA.

sources.title: Blender Python API Documentation
sources.verification: Primary API reference; version-specific behavior still needs runtime probing.
sources.claim: Authoritative source for bpy, bmesh, types, operators and version data.
sources.agent_use: Use API docs plus capability probes; do not trust remembered signatures.
sources.adopted: Yes: version/capability probe and source priority.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol documentation
sources.verification: Primary protocol documentation.
sources.claim: MCP standardizes discovery and invocation of tools/resources; it does not itself teach Blender artistry or guarantee safe execution.
sources.agent_use: Treat MCP as transport/tool contract, not skill memory.
sources.adopted: Yes: architecture distinction.

sources.title: Bridging Protocol and Production: Design Patterns for Deploying AI Agents with MCP
sources.verification: Field-informed design paper; enterprise client and some details are redacted.
sources.claim: Reliable production MCP needs explicit timeouts, structured errors, tool budgets, identity/context and observability beyond protocol basics.
sources.agent_use: Add deterministic error classes, budgets and logs.
sources.adopted: Yes: attempt limits and machine-readable stage failures.
